clue.text: Writer revising a book in Nevada

indicators.note: in places the reworked words inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NV is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nevada

indicators.note: revising a text rearranges it, so the letters of a book are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An author is rewriting a book while staying in Nevada.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an author at work in Nevada; the writer is the definition, and 'revising' is the anagram signal, with ABOKO the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote much of his work in America.

clue.text: Need a cycle? Give them a ring!

definitions.text: Need a cycle? Give them a ring!

parts.words: Need a cycle? Give them a ring!
parts.note: Wagner's opera cycle is the Ring of these dwarfs, who forged and fought over a magic ring

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an advert for a phone line; the cycle is Wagner's Ring cycle, named after these people.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's tetralogy is Der Ring des Nibelungen, about the dwarf race whose gold makes the ring.

clue.text: Where Cleary went south and Fitzgeraldrevisited

definitions.meaning: Jon Cleary wrote the novel ... South
F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote the story ... Revisited

explanation.walkthrough: Two titles: Jon Cleary's Babylon South and F. Scott Fitzgerald's Babylon Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Both book titles name the ancient Mesopotamian city, used as a byword for decadence.

clue.text: Coins paid for a sonata?

parts.note: Beethoven's violin sonata named after a violinist shares its name with old German coins

explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven dedicated his Violin Sonata No 9 to Rodolphe Kreutzer; the kreutzer was also a small coin in Germany and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The kreutzer was a small coin in southern Germany and Austria, and the name is also that of a Beethoven sonata.

clue.text: One known to Virginia — it's in Virginia!

indicators.note: in places the little word inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone acquainted with a woman named Virginia lives in the state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Virginia is Virginia Woolf, whose lover was Vita Sackville-West; the second is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Vita Sackville-West was Virginia Woolf's close friend and lover.

clue.text: Travelling primarily by car — as he did with 11

indicators.note: by sets the initial alongside, after the car maker

parts.note: Humber was a British make of car

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word Travelling is taken

explanation.surface: Someone motoring across country, just as a character did with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMBER was a British car maker. In the novel, Humbert Humbert drives across America with Lolita (11), so the definition is a description of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrator of Nabokov's novel takes the girl on a long road trip by car.

clue.text: Caribbean island on which pirates mutinied

definitions.meaning: the large West Indian island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic
the ship in Treasure Island on which Long John Silver's pirates rise against the captain

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the schooner in Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island holds Haiti and the Dominican Republic; Stevenson named his ship after it.

clue.text: Wooden detective? That's not right!

indicators.note: not right means the letter R for right is removed

parts.note: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's amateur detective

explanation.surface: A detective whose acting is stiff; surely that's wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a criticism of a detective's acting; it is the definition, as in made of a certain wood. R is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture made of the tree's timber can be called maple, as in a maple table.

clue.text: Miss Jong includes part of 9 that was written by Miss Nin

definitions.text: that was written by Miss Nin

indicators.note: includes means the novelist's name holds the abbreviation

parts.note: Erica Jong is the American author of Fear of Flying
OT, the Old Testament, is part of the Bible, the answer to 9

explanation.surface: One woman writer quotes scripture in work by another woman writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Anaïs Nin wrote the erotic collections Delta of Venus and Little Birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaïs Nin's best-known books are collections of sexually explicit short stories.

clue.text: Epithet embodying poor Athenian in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, the letters run across them

explanation.surface: A nickname partly captures a poor citizen of ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across epiTHET Embodying. Thetes were the lowest of Solon's four classes of Athenian citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens a thete was a member of the poorest property class of citizens.

clue.text: Good book with which to ruminate?

definitions.meaning: the Christian scriptures, often called the Good Book
a cow's third stomach, the omasum, is also known by this name, used in chewing the cud

explanation.walkthrough: To ruminate is to think, but here it is to chew the cud: the omasum of a ruminant is called by the same name as the scriptures because its folds look like the leaves of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The scriptures are known as the Good Book; ruminants' omasum takes the name from its page-like folds.

clue.text: I brood about Bell's creation and I'm furious

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so I plus the verb are read backwards

parts.note: to brood is to sit on eggs, so brood means sit
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone, so his creation is a phone

explanation.surface: Someone sits sulking near a telephone and announces they are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I SIT into TISI. 'I'm furious' is read cryptically: the speaker is one of the Furies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisiphone is one of the three Furies of Greek myth, so she could say she is one of the furious ones.

clue.text: 29 who gets whatever she wants? That's about it!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the name goes round the little word

parts.note: from the song 'Whatever Lola Wants, Lola Gets' in the musical Damn Yankees

explanation.surface: A girl who always gets what she wants; that's the whole story.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 29 across, NYMPHET. The song 'Whatever Lola Wants, Lola Gets' comes from the 1955 musical Damn Yankees.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's title character is the archetypal sexually precocious young girl.

clue.text: Leap madly about if dipping back into this novel

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so the turned little word goes into the other letters
madly means wildly mixed, so the letters of Leap are rearranged

parts.note: RE is Latin for about, concerning

indicators.note: back means the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone jumping about wildly before dipping back into a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leap madly about' looks like one picture of a jumper, but 'about' gives the Latin preposition RE. 'dipping' is the insertion signal; the definition is a Nabokov novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale Fire is a 1962 novel by Nabokov, built round a 999-line poem.

clue.text: "Her clothing coupons and were handed in at the Food Office" (John Betjeman)

definitions.text: "Her clothing coupons and were handed in at the Food Office" (John Betjeman)

parts.words: "Her clothing coupons and were handed in at the Food Office" (John Betjeman)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation: the missing words name the wartime booklet used to buy food

explanation.walkthrough: The gap after 'and' is filled by the answer: in Britain during and after the Second World War, households used these books to buy rationed food.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime British booklet of coupons for buying rationed foods was handed in at the Food Office.

clue.text: "Hapax legomenon" certainly encapsulates a type of word so qualified

definitions.text: a type of word so qualified
definitions.note: the adjective that describes a word coined for one occasion

indicators.note: encapsulates means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A Greek term for a word used only once clearly sums up one kind of word.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across legomeNON CErtainly. A hapax legomenon is a word recorded only once.
explanation.definitionFit: A word coined for a single occasion is called a nonce word, so it is qualified with this adjective.

clue.text: A Heston character faces druggies

parts.note: Charlton Heston played El Cid in the 1961 film
heads, as in the front faces of coins

explanation.surface: A character played by Charlton Heston confronts drug users.
explanation.walkthrough: Heston played the Spanish hero El Cid; the head of a coin is its face.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for habitual LSD users, acid being the drug's street name.

clue.text: Chap is involvedin disgraceful sham that involves pious practice

indicators.note: involved in means enclosed by, so the man's name and the little word go inside
disgraceful suggests something messed up, so the letters of sham are mixed

parts.note: Sid is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man is mixed up in a shameful fraud concerning religious observance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraceful' gives HASM, the reshuffled fraud, and 'involvedin' (involved in, printed as one word) puts the man and the little word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasidism is a Jewish pietist movement, its name from the Hebrew for pious.

clue.text: Academy where you might learn to polish wood? Boots more like!

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth and polish it
a hurst is an old word for a wood or wooded hill

explanation.surface: A college where you'd learn carpentry? More like boot-polishing!
explanation.walkthrough: SANDHURST is Britain's Royal Military Academy, where cadets famously spend hours polishing their boots, hence the joke at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst trains British Army officers.

clue.text: English endlessly agitated about soprano with irrational German musical drama

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the two pieces
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
endlessly means the last letter of English is cut off

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: An Englishman, worked up, holds forth on a singer and German theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final letter, 'agitated' turns the five-plus-one letters left into SINGEL, and 'about' wraps that round the singer's letter and the irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Singspiel is a German form of opera with spoken dialogue, such as Mozart's Magic Flute.

clue.text: They have eyes and stings

definitions.meaning: sewing implements each have a hole, an eye, for the thread
provokes or goads, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing tool has an eye for thread; to goad someone with remarks is to sting them.

clue.text: One's alter ego on good terms with a chap

parts.note: sir is a title for a man, a chap addressed politely
to be in with someone is to be on good terms with them

explanation.surface: Someone's other self gets along well with a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers to 1 across, Nabokov, who published his early Russian work as V. Sirin.
explanation.definitionFit: V. Sirin was the pen name the novelist used for his Russian-language books.

clue.text: Hermit mostly turning quiet, like Ingoldsby's jackdaw?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of Hermit

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A recluse goes silent, like a bird in a famous comic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts T from HERMIT and 'turning' makes RHEMI of the rest. The Ingoldsby Legends include 'The Jackdaw of Rheims'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhemish means of Rheims, the French city whose cardinal's ring the jackdaw stole.

clue.text: Very angry play by Nell Dunn?

definitions.meaning: Nell Dunn's 1981 comedy set in a Turkish bath

explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious is said to be fuming; Dunn's play is set in a Turkish bath, full of vapour.

clue.text: Ghostly subject of 12?

parts.note: the poet in Pale Fire, killed in the novel, bears a name meaning a ghost

explanation.walkthrough: In Pale Fire (12) the poem is by John Shade; a shade is also a ghost, and the poet dies in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: John Shade is the murdered poet in Nabokov's novel, and a spirit of the dead is a shade.

clue.text: Actor in Degrees of Separation finally

parts.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees
o' is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Separation is taken

explanation.surface: A performer appears in the film Six Degrees of Separation at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees of Separation' looks like a film title; it splits as MAS, O and N, from 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: James Mason was an English film star.

clue.text: Up-to-date interior design used by director about end of movie

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the director's name goes round the letter

parts.note: Hitch was the nickname of film director Alfred Hitchcock

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of movie is taken

explanation.surface: A film director uses modern interior décor around the end of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HITCH around E, the last letter given by 'end of' movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech is a design style using industrial materials and modern technology in the home.

clue.text: Book-classifying business could be uses this!

definitions.text: Book-classifying business could be uses this!

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of business might be rearranged into the two words

explanation.surface: A firm that sorts books might use this number.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the clue as a sum: the word for a firm, rearranged as 'could be' suggests, equals the word for employs plus this abbreviation, so the whole clue both defines and builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The International Standard Book Number identifies and classifies published books.

clue.text: In All Souls drunken lecturer drops indirect references

indicators.note: drunken means reeling, so the letters are mixed, with one letter left over

parts.note: L is short for lecturer, as on learner plates

explanation.surface: A tipsy Oxford don at All Souls College hints at things obliquely.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN ALL SOULS mixed up hold the answer plus L, which 'drops' removes. All Souls is an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusions mention something without naming it directly.

clue.text: This is about an erstwhile chemicals company taken over in a way that's extra-hostile

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: RE is Latin for about
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemicals giant

explanation.surface: A former chemicals firm suffers a hostile takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' reverses RE ICI, giving ICIER. 'Taken over' looks like a corporate takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy means cold and unfriendly, so a more icy manner is more hostile.

clue.text: Keynes puzzled about Catholic psychologist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the letter
puzzled means confused, so the letters of Keynes are muddled

explanation.surface: Economist Keynes is baffled by a Catholic psychologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzled' turns KEYNES into EYSENK, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Eysenck was a German-born British psychologist known for his theory of personality.

clue.text: Doll perhaps, friend of Falstaff, sulks about Hal's initiation

parts.note: Corporal Nym is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sulk goes round the letter

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, the sulks

indicators.note: initiation means the start, so the first letter of Hal's is taken

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean drinking companion is in a huff about Prince Hal's beginnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Nym, Falstaff's friend, appears in Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor. 'about' puts PET around H, from 'initiation' of Hal's.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll is slang for an attractive young woman, and a nymphet is a sexually attractive girl.
